{"id": "a7e1d3d0-0915-4786-9c21-7e786dec0de3", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Confirmed — no, you can't conclude that from `ListDistributions` alone.

Looking at the actual `DistributionSummary` object returned by `ListDistributions`, there's **no `Logging` field at all**. It includes things like `Aliases`, `Origins`, `DefaultCacheBehavior`, `ViewerCertificate`, `WebACLId`, `Restrictions`, `Staging`, `AnycastIpListId`, etc. — but standard access logging config (bucket, prefix, `IncludeCookies`, enabled flag) simply isn't part of the summary shape.

To check whether access logging is enabled, you need the full distribution config, via either:
- `GetDistribution` (returns `Distribution.DistributionConfig.Logging`), or
- `GetDistributionConfig` (returns `DistributionConfig.Logging` directly)

So for an operational review, absence of a logging indicator in `ListDistributions` output means nothing — you'd have to call `GetDistributionConfig` per distribution ID to get a real answer.

If you're doing this across your account's distributions, I can pull that for you — want me to check which of your CloudFront distributions actually have access logging enabled?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
